headline: High-risk shared-workspace and broad-egress orchestration can leak or corrupt data; prompt-injection risk is low because the collection profile is non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable content collection profile, so it does not ingest B’s outputs by default. Agent B can process files and workflow nodes, but no shared instruction channel is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or file handoff, which keeps the injection surface limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B-generated text into A-facing prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared message queue or MCP bridge is added later, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A as a read-only reference source.
Avoid copying untrusted B output into prompts.
Use a strict template for any manual handoff.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workflow artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B reads and writes the server filesystem and has broad network egress, while A is a docs-only collection profile with no data classes touched. The pair can still leak workflow contents if B processes sensitive files on the shared server; A does not add a second exfiltration path, but B alone is enough for medium risk.
conditions: IF the workflow processes sensitive files on the n8n server, B can transmit them outward.
IF A is repurposed to store user content locally, shared-server exposure increases.
mitigations: Restrict B workflows to non-sensitive inputs.
Disable or scope outbound integrations.
Store secrets outside the workflow filesystem.
Review file paths before execution.
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive jobs onto a separate host.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capability, but B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses on a shared execution host. That creates a real conflict surface if both touch the same workspace or artifacts, even though A itself is not writable. Uncertainty about the exact shared directory layout pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same workspace directory, concurrent artifact corruption becomes possible.
IF multiple B instances run against shared state, write conflicts increase.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes in the orchestrator.
Use per-run filenames.
Check for stale artifacts before execution.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static collection profile, so it does not generate authoritative facts for B to act on. However, B’s AI Agent/workflow model can still treat imported content as trusted if an operator feeds A-derived material into a workflow node. The pathway exists, but it is not default and lacks evidence of automatic action chaining.
conditions: IF an operator feeds A-derived text into a B workflow node without verification, B may act on it.
IF B is configured to send emails or trigger integrations from unverified inputs, downstream errors cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before action nodes.
Add validation steps between input and execution.
Label A-derived content as untrusted.
Limit auto-send integrations.
requires-engineering: enforce schema checks on workflow inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated data class is documented for A, while B explicitly handles workflow data on the n8n server and may route it through integrations. Because the pair lacks a documented mismatch such as EU-to-US or PHI handling, only a small compliance gap is evidenced here.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated data classes, compliance review is required.
IF an integration node sends data to a non-compliant destination, the gap widens.
mitigations: Classify data before enabling workflows.
Restrict integrations to approved destinations.
Review retention settings.
Document residency for each node.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement per workflow.
